headline: AI made senior developers 19% slower. They believed it made them 20% faster.

slides.html:
AI made senior developers 19% slower.

They believed it made them 20% faster.

A randomised study · real repos · real engineers

METR · Feb–Jun 2025

Not a survey.
A controlled experiment.

Developers16, experienced
Tasks246 real issues
Codebases1M+ lines, 22k+ ★
ToolsCursor + Claude 3.5/3.7

Each task was randomly assigned: AI allowed or AI not allowed. Then they measured the time.

What they expected, felt — and what happened

A 39-point gap between how productive they felt and how productive they were.

Feeling productive is not the same as being productive.

If you lead engineers, this is the real risk: sprint plans, estimates and headcount decisions built on how fast AI feels.

The people closest to the work were wrong about their own speed — by a lot.

METR follow-up · Feb 2026

The tools got better. Measuring got harder.

57 developers, 800+ tasks. Early estimates now point to a speed-up — about 18% for returning developers, 4% for new ones.

But METR calls it very weak evidence. Many developers no longer wanted to work without AI, and 30–50% said they held back tasks they didn't want to do without it.

Measure AI like any other change

01

Baseline before rollout. Cycle time, lead time, rework — captured before anyone changes tools.

02

Compare like with like. Similar tasks, similar size, same team.

03

Track quality, not just speed. Review time, defects, reverted changes.

04

Treat “it feels faster” as a hypothesis. Then test it.

Remember this

Self-reported AI productivity is unreliable — even from experts.

AI may well make your team faster. You won't know unless you measure.

The question isn’t “are we using AI?” It’s “what changed in delivery?”

Has AI made your team faster — or does it just feel that way?

How do you actually know? Tell me in the comments.
